We're one of the largest early investors in Polymarket, and this story that Shayne was "caught red-handed" using company money is just a flat out garbage hit piece.

Shayne wasn't taking a salary. He was 21 when he started Polymarket, he was living hand-to-mouth running the company out of his apartment, barely making ends meet when he was raising his seed round. We were his first term sheet and literally offered to loan him money personally, but he ended up not needing it when the seed round came together.

After COVID and the crazy Biden-era crackdown on crypto that was happening at the time, there was a lot of chaos in almost every company in the industry. As an investor, we saw a lot of companies go through pandemic-era startup craziness, and Polymarket was no exception.

But Shayne disclosed every dollar he spent, which turned out to annualize to about a software engineer's salary. That's including the flights, none of which were personal flights. Plus, SHAYNE STARTED the accounting and payback process, no one “found” it. In aggregate, it was nothing that an investor would balk at. He paid it back to the company in full, and then got on a normal salary like everyone else.

It was an accounting problem, not an integrity problem. It was not a big deal.

Polymarket has had growing pains, no doubt. It went from a small fledging startups to one of the most explosive consumer brands in America. But Shayne has leveled up alongside the company, and as investors we have total confidence in him.

Enough of this stupid FUD.

The end.

Speculation has always had two engines.

New technology makes the future look bigger than the present. Britain’s railways in the 1840s and the internet in the 1990s both ran on that engine.

Political and monetary strain pushes people toward long shots by making the ordinary path to wealth feel out of reach. In 1720 the public piled into South Sea Company shares that had been swapped for Britain’s war debt. In the 2000s the bet was a home bought with an easy mortgage.

The famous bubbles mostly ran on one engine at a time. Today both are running hard together.

AI is driving the largest private build in decades. The four biggest hyperscalers guided to $720B to $745B of capex for 2026.

Meanwhile, the social contract has been broken. A strained political and monetary order has culminated in a deficit that sits near 6% of GDP with no recession, and a home costs 3.5x the income of a household under 40.

The bets followed. Legal US sports betting grew about 25x from 2018 to 2025. Kalshi and Polymarket’s monthly volume matched that in a single year.

The things being bet on will keep changing names. The crowd will keep needing somewhere to bet.
